title: Farmer / Cow / Dog / God Deep Cartography
core_correction: Farmer and Cow are the primary relational pair inside the Farm. Dog and God are not alternative Farm-role labels for Cow/Farmer. In the project's theology, Dog/God describes Tim's relation to the same Farmer: the Farmer is a human participant in the Farm, while Dog/God is a higher relational and symbolic axis through which Tim is interpreted in relation to that Farmer.

farm_relations.farmer: The Farmer is the relational counterpart of the Cow inside the Farm: cultivation, observation, harvesting, framing, attention and interpretation occur between Farmer and Cow.
farm_relations.cow: The Cow is the subject around which the Farmer's cultivation and attention organize. Cow is a structural/project term, not a diagnosis or statement of human worth.
farm_relations.important_rule: Do not collapse Farmer and Dog into one taxonomy. Farmer/Cow describes the Farm relationship. Dog/God describes a different theological relation involving Tim and the Farmer.

tim_relations.farmer: Within the project's Potatoist theology, Tim's relation to the Farmer can be represented through the paired language Dog/God. This is a symbolic-theological relation, not a claim of supernatural control over identifiable people.
tim_relations.dog: Dog is the lower/mud-facing relational image in Tim's relation to the Farmer: the watcher, boundary creature, earth-near figure and warning image. The biblical Dog vocabulary must be read before assigning this symbol a modern psychological meaning.
tim_relations.god: God is the higher/source relation: the Most High, Father and judging/ordering source in the project's canon. God and Dog are therefore a vertical pair in the Tim/Farmer relationship rather than two Farm occupations.
tim_relations.pair: God ↕ Dog — Tim's vertical relation to the Farmer
tim_relations.distinction: Farmer/Cow is horizontal Farm relation; God/Dog is vertical theological relation.

mud_dweller.definition: Within the project's theology, a mud dweller is a dweller who remains oriented toward the mud/earthly lower condition rather than turning toward the upward/root/sprout path. Mud dwelling is therefore a spiritual posture or choice in the canon, not a claim that a real person literally lives in supernatural mud.
mud_dweller.dweller: A dweller is one who inhabits a plane. In the project's dimensional language, the mud dweller is defined by continued dwelling in the lower material/strife condition rather than merely passing through it.
mud_dweller.choice: The theological point is agency: dwelling is not simply the existence of mud. It is the repeated choice to remain identified with what the mud rewards.
mud_dweller.serpent_relation: The serpent is the archetypal mechanism associated with the mud-dwelling choice because Genesis places the serpent under a curse of belly-crawling and dust-eating after the deception in Eden. This is a project interpretation of the biblical pattern, not a claim that every mud dweller is literally possessed by a serpent.
mud_dweller.inverse: The opposite movement is not hatred of matter. It is transformation: mud → root → potato → sprout → tree → fruit.

biblical_grounding.genesis_3_14: Genesis 3:14 explicitly places the serpent on its belly and associates its existence with eating dust. The project's mud-dweller metaphor draws from this image.
biblical_grounding.genesis_3_15: Genesis 3:15 establishes enmity between the serpent and the woman/offspring and therefore supplies the project's deeper conflict pattern: serpent-line versus life-line.
biblical_grounding.genesis_2_7: Humanity is formed from dust/ground in the Genesis creation account. This makes dust symbolically important: the serpent eats what humanity was formed from, while humanity is called toward life rather than merely remaining dust.
biblical_grounding.isaiah_56_10_11: Isaiah's 'dogs' are attached to failed watchmen: blind, silent, sleepy and driven by appetite/self-gain. This is critical to the project's Dog interpretation because the Dog is not automatically virtuous. A watchdog can fail its function and become hungry, blind or self-serving.
biblical_grounding.philippians_3_2: Philippians uses 'dogs' as a warning term. In the project this reinforces the boundary/warning dimension of Dog symbolism.
biblical_grounding.revelation_22_15: Revelation places 'dogs' outside the holy city alongside those characterized by falsehood and other excluded practices. The project reads this symbolically as a boundary between the lower pattern and the restored order.
biblical_grounding.interpretive_rule: Biblical passages are evidence for the symbolic genealogy of the project's theology, not proof that contemporary individuals are literally biblical characters.

dog_deep_reading.not_a_pet_symbol: The biblical Dog is not reducible to loyalty, friendship or a modern domestic-pet metaphor.
dog_deep_reading.boundary: Dog can signify boundary, exclusion, warning and proximity to what is outside the holy order.
dog_deep_reading.appetite: Isaiah 56 makes appetite central: dogs are described as having strong appetites and never being satisfied, while the shepherds seek their own gain. This connects Dog to the project's earlier Hunger/Greed shadow, but it should be treated as biblical symbolism rather than diagnosis.
dog_deep_reading.failed_watchman: The most important Dog inversion is the mute or blind watchman. A Dog that should bark may instead sleep; a guardian can become an appetite-driven participant.
dog_deep_reading.return: 2 Peter 2:22 uses the dog returning to its own vomit as an image of repetitive return. In the project's system this can represent the Farm's return to old conflict after apparent resolution.
dog_deep_reading.warning: The same symbol can therefore contain guardian and shadow: watchfulness can become appetite; warning can become accusation; protection can become pursuit.

farmer_cow_dynamics.farmer: Cultivates attention around the Cow; may document, interpret, react, archive, monetize or attempt to understand.
farmer_cow_dynamics.cow: Provides the visible subject around which Farm attention organizes; may react to Farmers and thereby create additional material.
feedback_loop: Cow responds or continues public activity
expanded archive changes how future Cow events are interpreted
farmer_cow_dynamics.inversion: Farmer can become Cow when the Farm's attention shifts toward the Farmer. Cow can become Farmer when the subject begins cultivating an audience around the Farm itself.
farmer_cow_dynamics.stopping_condition: A healthy research relationship has a stopping condition: sufficient evidence, correction, proportionality, resolution or disengagement. Extraction has no inherent stopping condition.

seven_deadly_sins.historical_note: The familiar seven-sin taxonomy is a Christian tradition rather than a seven-item biblical list. It developed from earlier monastic accounts of evil thoughts and was reorganized in the Western tradition; modern scholarship also treats the sins as a useful taxonomy of recurring temptations.

sins.name: Pride
sins.tim_shadow: the lower relation mistakes its own judgment for the source

sins.name: Greed / Avarice
sins.tim_shadow: the source relation is inverted into ownership

sins.name: Envy
sins.tim_shadow: the relation is interpreted through scarcity

demonology_as_archetype.rule: Demons are symbolic names for recurring patterns of temptation and inversion. The repository must not turn them into unsupported claims about supernatural possession of real people.

principal_forms.name: The Prosecutor
principal_forms.temptation: turn moral knowledge into unlimited punishment

principal_forms.name: The Hunger
principal_forms.temptation: prevent the attention cycle from ending

principal_forms.name: The Serpent
principal_forms.temptation: remain in the mud/dust orientation through deception, appetite and misdirected desire

demonology_as_archetype.theological_pattern: The serpent is the primordial inversion image in the project's mud model: the creature associated with deception becomes bound to belly and dust, while the human story is directed toward conflict with the serpent and toward life beyond mere dust.

psychological_engine.moral_disengagement: Bandura's framework identifies moral justification, sanitizing language, advantageous comparison, diffusion/displacement of responsibility, minimizing consequences, victim blaming and dehumanization as mechanisms by which moral self-sanctions can be disengaged.
farm_translation: I'm exposing them for the public good.
Whatever happens is their own fault.
The target is only a lolcow/object/enemy.
psychological_engine.darvo: DARVO must be recorded as an evidenced sequence rather than assigned as a personality label.

hawkins_consciousness_map.sequence: Shame → Guilt → Apathy → Grief → Fear → Desire → Anger → Pride → Courage → Neutrality → Willingness → Acceptance → Reason → Love → Joy → Peace
hawkins_consciousness_map.rule: Never assign a Hawkins level to a real person as if it were validated psychology.
hawkins_consciousness_map.farm_question: Which state does the Farmer/Cow relationship reward?
hawkins_consciousness_map.tim_question: Which state does the God/Dog relation symbolically call the Farmer away from or toward?

relational_diagram.full: God/Tim → Dog → Farmer ↔ Cow → Farm → Mud
relational_diagram.return: Mud → Root → Potato → Sprout → Tree → Fruit → Life
relational_diagram.serpent: Serpent → deception/appetite → mud/dust orientation → dwelling; the canonical counter-movement is truth, restraint, root, sprout and life

research_rule: From this point onward, every Farm profile must distinguish the Farmer/Cow relation from the Tim/God/Dog relation. Dog must be researched through the biblical corpus before being reduced to modern internet 'watchdog' language.
